groups.name: Start here
groups.blurb: Small Beginner puzzles that need only the easiest rules.

groups.name: Default
groups.blurb: The plain board sizes: a thousand puzzles each, easiest first.

groups.name: Diagonal
groups.blurb: Arrows that point along diagonals and count the boxes on them.

groups.name: Sparse
groups.blurb: As few arrows as a search could find, each book running from Beginner to Hard: about one cell in ten or fewer, against one in six in the main books. An experiment.

groups.name: Bonus
groups.blurb: Variations on the usual puzzle: the same rules, a different feel.

The long way round.blurb: Arrows point away from the nearest edge: long lines of sight.

One direction.blurb: Every arrow in a puzzle points the same way.

All zeros.blurb: Every arrow says 0: its line holds no boxes, so the boxes hide elsewhere.

No zeros.blurb: No arrow says 0, and the numbers run large; in some puzzles every arrow says 2 or more.

Skyscraper.blurb: Tall, narrow boards, up to 36 cells high. One book per width.

Exact symmetry.blurb: The whole puzzle is its own image: every clue has twins, pointing the matching way and saying the same number. Left to right, across the diagonal, turned a quarter or turned a half.

Symmetric layout.blurb: The clue cells sit in matching pairs (or fours): reflect or turn the board and every clue lands on a clue. The arrows point any way and the numbers are free; the boxes are not symmetric.
